function.name: cmd_controller_execute
function.description: Executes a system-level command using os.system() on Windows operating systems. It can execute single or multiple commands chained with '&&'. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

command.description: The system command to be executed. To execute multiple commands, separate them with '&&'. For example, 'dir && echo done'.

unit.description: Specifies the unit of measure for the command if applicable. This is not utilized by os.system() directly but can be used for logging or analysis purposes.

message.reasoning: The user asks: "is chrome is installed". They want to know if Chrome is installed on the system. We can use the provided function to run a command to check if Chrome is installed. On Windows, Chrome is typically installed in Program Files or Program Files (x86). We can check existence of chrome.exe. Use where command: "where chrome" or "where chrome.exe". Or check registry. But simplest: use "where chrome" which returns path if found. So we can call cmd_controller_execute with command "where chrome". Then parse output. But we cannot parse output; we just return the result of the command. The function will execute and return whatever. We can then interpret. But we need to respond to user. We can run the command.
